name: application-media-object-row
title: Media Object Row
description: Reusable media-row primitive — thumbnail, title, meta line, and a trailing action slot — for lists of media-backed items like episodes, files, or tracks.
useWhen: Listing items that each have a thumbnail/cover image, a title, a short metadata line, and one primary action — podcast episodes, tracks, files, videos.
You want a lightweight, reusable row primitive rather than a full table for media-centric lists.
The trailing action varies per item (play, download, more menu) — pass `renderAction` to customize it per row.
avoidWhen: Rows need multiple columns of comparable data (size, date modified, owner) — use `tables` or `details-list` instead.
The list represents team/role membership rather than media — use `team-members-list` for that semantic instead.
There's no image/thumbnail to anchor the row — a plain text list avoids the unused image slot.
responsiveBehavior: Thumbnail, text column, and trailing action sit in a single flex row; the title/meta column truncates with an ellipsis rather than wrapping, keeping row height constant at any width.
accessibility: The thumbnail image's alt text is empty by default (decorative) since the title conveys the same information as text; pass imageAlt when the image carries unique meaning.
The default trailing play button has an aria-label that includes the item's title, not a generic "Play", since every row shares the same icon-only button.
Title and meta are separate text nodes so screen readers announce them distinctly rather than as one run-on string.

variants.title: Media Object Row
variants.description: Three podcast episode rows with thumbnail, title, episode/duration meta, and a play button.
accessibility: The renderAction slot lets callers swap in any accessible control (download, menu) while keeping the row's semantic structure intact.

variants.title: Media Object Row (Dark)
variants.description: Media object row list adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Text and divider colors are tuned to meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark surface.
